# Decisions: repo-memory-capture

- 2026-08-04T09:31:30.714Z — chose **A dedicated promotion affordance for operational knowledge: a new memory_promoted event (payload {text}), captured via `sofar remember` and the sofar_remember MCP tool, addressable as `<slug> M<n>` in the existing citation grammar, with doctor's repo-memory axis warning when a promoted memory is not named in .sofar/repo.md. repo.md stays hand-written; doctor still only detects.** over Making notes citable so the existing observed-citation axis fires on them; and adding only symptom detectors (repo.md untouched across N closed initiatives, or files and commands recurring cross-initiative that repo.md never names). because record-graph rejected a scope:repo|initiative field on decision_logged because a decision's generality is not knowable at log time — decisions BECOME general later — and a declared field would be blind to every decision already in the record. That reasoning is about decisions and does not transfer to operational procedure: the release command's repo-wide scope was known the moment it was learned, there is nothing to wait for, and no amount of citation behaviour will ever surface a fact that was never written down anywhere. Both observed-only alternatives fail the case that prompted this — the publish command lived in private tool memory, produced no artifact, and would have stayed invisible under either. This is declaration, but of a different proposition: not "this decision is repo-wide" but "this fact is repo memory", which only its author can know and which no derivation can recover.
- 2026-08-04T09:45:09.175Z — chose **M&lt;n&gt; is opt-in in extractCitations — a `{ memories: true }` option that only the repo.md scan passes — and promoted memories are NOT graph nodes in this initiative.** over Adding M&lt;n&gt; to the grammar unconditionally, and the fuller alternative of minting memory nodes in buildGraph so decisions could cite promotions and resolve them. because The grammar has two callers with opposite needs. The repo.md scan reads qualified handles and never resolves, so a wider grammar costs it nothing. Decision prose is resolved against real nodes, and since promotions have none, an unconditional M&lt;n&gt; would turn every legitimate mention of a memory into a dangling entry — manufacturing exactly the false signal record-graph 5.3 removed for BD&lt;n&gt;. Node-minting is the coherent end state and would fix that properly, but it widens buildGraph, resolveCitation, why and related for a capability nobody asked for yet; the detection the gap actually needs works without it. Left as a pending Phase 4 task rather than half-built.
